name_en: Jin Si Huang Ju (Golden Thread Chrysanthemum)
processing: Whole flower heads are selected and dried with machine heat, often at the farm where they grow. The first flush of big blooms goes to flower tea.
harvest_season: Late autumn: in Xiushui the fields were in full bloom in mid-November 2025. Larger blooms are picked first and smaller ones are left a few days to open.
appearance_dry: Large, flat whole flower heads with fine golden-yellow petals around a darker centre.
appearance_liquor: Clear, bright yellow, typical of yellow chrysanthemum infusions.
appearance_wet: The whole flower floats and spreads open, with slender soft yellow petals.
taste_profile: As with other tea chrysanthemums, expect a floral aroma with light sweetness and a faint herbal edge; little specific tasting detail is documented for this variety.

brewing.notes: Usually one flower to a tall glass, so the bloom can open. Top up with hot water as you drink, as is customary with chrysanthemum.

vintage_note: Sold after the autumn harvest as dried whole flowers, in boxes or by weight, and as with other flower teas it is best within about a year. Price follows flower size and how intact the heads are. Regional names such as Wuyuan huangju are sold alongside it at different prices.
description:
Jin Si Huang Ju is a large-flowered golden chrysanthemum grown for the cup, sold as whole dried heads. The name means roughly imperial chrysanthemum of golden threads, and the fine petals are the point: one flower can fill a glass.

Farms pick the big blooms first, then dry them, often in on-site drying rooms. Xiushui County in northern Jiangxi is a major area, reported at 18,000 mu in 2025 and about 900 tons of dried flowers a year. Guanyun and Hongze in Jiangsu also grow it.

The taste is less documented than the look. Like other tea chrysanthemums it should be floral and gently sweet, with a pale to bright yellow liquor. Use a glass or wide cup, because a cramped pot wastes the appearance and may tear the petals.

When buying, look for whole heads with few loose petals and a clean floral smell. Compare the place named on the box, as the same trade name covers flowers from several provinces.
history: This is a recent commercial crop as far as records go. In Xiushui, one grower is reported to have started planting it in 2011, and the county's industry grew in later years through company and farmer partnerships, with sales abroad reported to 12 countries. Little is documented about where the variety itself came from.
